# Spec review (independent, PR-facing)

**Concise, compact, facts only.**

Criteria and output shape: `ferrule guide show reviewer --section 'Axes, reported separately' --section 'Spec changes' --section Output`; this skill supplies gate 3's *inputs* for a reviewer outside the implementing session.

## Gather inputs — no shared session

- **Ticket** — `ferrule issue view <n> --comments`. The ticket is self-contained: the issue's `## Requirements` (local IDs) and `## Scenarios` are the spec as filed, its comments the changes kept since; the PR body (`ferrule pr view <n>`) maps local to fixed IDs (`## Requirements`, Issue column) and holds `## Architecture` and `## Decisions`. Changes classified as detail are only on the branch, in `docs/specs/`.
- **Branch/PR** — from the ticket's linked PR, or ask the user for PR number/branch.
- **Base ref** — the PR's target branch.

## Run the review

`ferrule run init <slug>` for a scratch run directory. Write the ticket's normative text into its `spec-diff.md` (one `## S<n> — <title>` section per scenario, one `## <ID> — <kind>` section per row of the PR's `## Requirements` table, the approved changes from the comments applied, same shape as gate 1) and the PR's `## Architecture` into `architecture.md` (the table → `## Components`, `Public surface:` → `## Public surface`; the PR has no interfaces) with its `## Decisions`, so the reviewer reads them the way it reads every run's; `review.md` and `review.verdict.md` land there too. Spawn `fe-reviewer` with: scope `branch`, the base ref, the run directory's absolute path, the checkout path. No `plan.md` and no stage cards exist on this side — say so: no stage ids, every finding's stage column is `—`. The ticket's spec with its approved comments applied is the approved baseline. Give it nothing more, never the issue/PR number. It answers with a status line only.

A fresh session may review inline with the same axes and rigor; a session that implemented any of it spawns.

## Output

Point the developer at `review.verdict.md` (`ferrule prompt show <file>`), the full `review.md` on request. Then `ferrule run cleanup <slug>`.

## Stop condition

Report and stop. Approving is the developer's own gate before manual QA and merge — no PR edits, no merge.
